note.text:
Simple distillation separates a liquid (the solvent) from a solution, keeping the liquid.
The solution is boiled in a flask; the vapour passes into a Liebig condenser cooled by cold water (in at the bottom, out at the top); it condenses and drips into a receiver as the distillate. The dissolved solid stays in the flask.
Use: pure (distilled) water from salt water or tap water.
Fractional distillation separates liquids that mix but have different boiling points, using a fractionating column. The liquid with the lower boiling point distils first.
Uses: ethanol (78 °C) from water (100 °C); petrol, kerosene and diesel from crude oil; gases from liquid air.
The thermometer bulb is placed at the side arm to read the temperature of the vapour.

worked_example.problem: A mixture of {a} (boiling point {ta} °C) and {b} ({tb} °C) is fractionally distilled. Which distils first?
steps: The liquid with the lower boiling point boils first.

cards.idea: Simple distillation gets the liquid back from a solution: boil, then condense the vapour.
example: The salt stays in the flask.

cards.idea: In the condenser, cold water goes in at the bottom and out at the top; the vapour condenses to the distillate.
example: The condenser is a Liebig condenser.
The liquid collected is the distillate.

cards.idea: Fractional distillation separates liquids that mix; the lower boiling point comes off first.

check.prompt: A mixture of {X.a} (boiling point {X.ta} °C) and {X.b} ({X.tb} °C) is fractionally distilled. Which distils first?

misconceptions.explain: That liquid has the higher boiling point; it distils later.
They have different boiling points, so they distil one after the other.

solution: The lower boiling point is reached first.

pick.q: Which method gives pure water from salt water?
e: Decanting does not remove dissolved salt.

pick.q: In simple distillation of salt water, where is the salt at the end?
e: Only the water reaches the receiver.

pick.q: What is the liquid collected in distillation called?
e: The residue stays in the flask or filter.
The solute is the dissolved solid.
pick.y: The condensed liquid is the distillate.

pick.q: Where does the cold water enter the condenser?
e: Entering at the bottom fills the jacket completely.
pick.y: In at the bottom, out at the top.

pick.q: Where should the thermometer bulb be in distillation?
pick.r: at the side arm of the flask
w: in the liquid at the bottom
e: It must read the vapour temperature.
That only shows the cooling water.
pick.y: It reads the temperature of the vapour leaving.

right.text: Distilled water is made by simple distillation.
Crude oil is separated by fractional distillation.
The distillate is collected in the receiver.
The liquid with the lower boiling point distils first.

wrong.text: Cold water enters the condenser at the top.
wrong.explain: It enters at the bottom so the jacket fills.

wrong.text: Filtration gives pure water from salt water.
wrong.explain: The dissolved salt passes through the filter.

wrong.text: The thermometer bulb is put in the boiling liquid.
wrong.explain: It is placed at the side arm to read the vapour temperature.
